sentences.text:
This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 31/01/2011 passed by the First Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Gwalior (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal")
in Claim Case No.162/2009, on the grounds of inadequacy of compensation as well as total exoneration of the Insurance Company from its liability.

entities.text: First Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant seeks enhancement of compensation and setting aside of the findings absolving the Insurance Company.
2. The date of accident and the issue of negligence are not in dispute.
The dispute pertains only to the question of liability and quantum of compensation.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4778 2 MA-655-2011 3.
As per the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal, due to injury sustained by appellant-Rajendra Nath Dubey in the motor accident in question.
The Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.40,700/- along with interest.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the Claims Tribunal committed an error in awarding compensation, as the amount awarded is on the lower side.

It was contended that Rajendra Nath Dubey vs Paramjeet on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38506023/
1 the Claims Tribunal failed to award compensation under other permissible heads such as mental agony and special diet.

sentences.text: It was further submitted that at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid driving licence and, therefore, the Claims Tribunal completely exonerated the Insurance Company from its liability.

It was argued that the claimant is a third party and, as such, the Insurance Company is statutorily liable to pay compensation to the claimant, with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly, a prayer was made for enhancement of compensation to a just and reasonable amount and for issuance of a direction to the Insurance Company to pay the compensation to the claimant with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company supported the impugned award and submitted that the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation based on the evidence available on record.
It is contended that the appeal lacks merit and deserves dismissal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4778 3 MA-655-2011 Tribunal.
7.
It is undisputed that appellant/claimant is third party and it is also undisputed that at the time of accident, driver of offending vehicle had no driving licence.

Therefore, it is clear cut of breach of insurance policy but in the light of Sohan Lal Passi v. P. Sesh Reddy , (1996) 5 SCC 21; National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Swaran Singh & Ors. , (2004) 3 SCC 297; and United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
v. Lehru & Ors. , (2003) 3 SCC 338 , the Insurance Company is under a statutory obligation to satisfy the award in respect of third-party liability, with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 8. Consequently, the Claims Tribunal committed an error in totally exonerating the Insurance Company from liability.

The impugned award is, therefore, modified to the extent that the Insurance Company shall pay the compensation to the claimant with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

9. In respect of enhancement of compensation amount is concerned, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, more particularly the injuries and permanent disability sustained by claimant in the alleged accident, it would be appropriate to enhance to lump sum amount of Rs.75,000/-
10.
Accordingly, present appeal is allowed in part to the extent indicated herein above.
The amount of compensation is enhanced to lump sum amount of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) in the present appeal.
The appellant is entitled to receive Rs.75,000/- in addition to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4778 4 MA-655-2011 the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of its petition till its realization.
It is made clear that appellant/claimant shall get interest from the date of deposit of court fee.
